mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle, compressing discount rates applied to equity cash flows and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in unemployment rate above 3.6% triggers negative S&P 500 forward returns within 5 trading days due to heightened inflation expectations.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns despite UNRATE crossing above 3.6pp

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous expansion in both demand (GDPC1) and supply (INDPRO) above historical averages signals robust economic growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and INDPRO both exceed 12-month averages by 5%
failure_condition: Rank IC < 0.05 over 60d window despite both proxies rising

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5% during a monetary tightening cycle, S&P 500 forward returns turn negative over the subsequent 20 trading days due to elevated borrowing costs.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.5% in a tightening cycle
failure_condition: SPX returns positive when FEDFUNDS >4.5% in tightening phase

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent increases in labor participation (PAYEMS) and demand (GDPC1) above historical levels signal robust economic activity, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and GDPC1 both exceed 12-month averages by 5%
failure_condition: returns negative despite both proxies rising

failure_condition: returns positive when CPIAUCSL spikes above 254.958
